analysis: Both changed files are test-only (ClusterOwnerServingTests.swift, ClusterPairServingDecisionsTests.swift). No production code, auth, crypto, attestation, or data-handling paths change, so none can regress in this diff. The new tests encode intended behavior of the owner-declared public-model path (ClusterPublicModels.declared, publicTrafficLine with publicModels/tensorAssistant parameters, ownerServing().declaredFamilies, ClusterPairOwnerServing.tensorAssistantNotOffered): a declared model is reported as 'qualified for public traffic' in its declared families (pipeline and tensor parallel) without qualification records, but only for the declared artifact SHA, not for other artifacts, undeclared families (pipelineMTP, phaseSplit) or undeclared models. A speculative-assistant placement is reported as 'not offered for public traffic'. Existing tests are updated to pass publicModels: [] to isolate record-only behavior. These tests are consistent with fail-closed semantics, covering artifact binding and family restriction. The production changes they imply (not supplied here) are relevant to T-007 and T-054 style trust assumptions: declaring models public without local parity records relies on the coordinator's parity qualification ('the coordinator's parity qualification decides each placement'). That coordinator-side enforcement is outside the supplied evidence and platform-owned. The next pass should verify, in the production source, that the declared public grant cannot be offered to the coordinator for the assistant path or for non-declared artifacts, and that the publicTrafficLine text is informational and does not itself grant routing. No findings are raised, since the production implementation is not visible and test-only changes add no attack surface.
